context: Dual-axis weather station chart showing daily temperature (line, left axis) and weekly rainfall (bars, right axis) over 18 months with sensor gaps explicitly marked
first_impression: Exemplary gap handling dominates the design — segmented lines with dashed bridges, labeled gap regions, and hatched bars for missing rainfall are all handled honestly and transparently.
what_works: Gap handling is best-in-class: temperature is manually segmented to avoid false continuity, with dashed bridges, boundary markers, and gap labels; rainfall gaps use hatched bars and null filtering. Rainfall bars correctly start at zero; the non-zero temperature baseline uses a data-driven extent with a zigzag broken-axis indicator and a bottom-of-chart caution note explicitly warning dual-axis scales are independent.
what_doesnt: Dual-axis correlation risk remains despite the warning — a reader can still visually fabricate correlation by comparing the two series. Data joins lack key functions (no `.data(data, d => d.id)`), so a live-update scenario would risk visual corruption, though this is not an issue for the current static render.
